newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas lurches up with more cold-inspired buying.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas lurches up with more cold-inspired buying.

text.p: The U.K. natural gas market lurched higher again on Wednesday as heavy buying by a handful of major players stoked the rally triggered earlier in the week by a sharp downturn in temperatures, traders said.
"It's a spooked market," said one trader. "It's a follow-through to the colder weather... There's a couple of guys frightening the market by leading up the bids."
Trade was spread fairly evenly across the forward curve, but traders said that the first quarter 1997 was leading the ascent.
"The main bit that's ramping up is Q1," said one trader.
The first quarter 1997 was confirmed traded at 19.25 pence a therm (p/th), and values were rumoured to have pushed up to 19.50 p/th by late in the day.
The prompt market was also bid up aggressively, with within day gas traded above 18 p/th. Dec values also rocketed to 17.50 p/th.
In contrast to Tuesday, the flexibility mechanism saw heavy system selling early in the day, shippers said.
Around nine million therms was believed to have been sold at an average price of around 13.5-14 p/th.

"It was totally overbought," said one major shipper. "Last night they were at the point of asking people to interrupt (deliveries to end-users) and now all these sells. You wonder about the forecasting."
But another trader predicted that the system would be again be short towards the end of the gas day.
"The skies are clearing and we're expecting (temperatures) to go down to minus four (degrees) tonight (in the Southeast)..The system will certainly be being bought later," he said.

TransCo confirmed that on Tuesday, the gas day November 19, the flexibility mechanism bought a total of 7,775,653 kilowatt hours (265,471 therms) at an average price of 1.4652 pence per kilowatt hour (42.915 pence a therm). Traders said that flex volumes were bought as high as 58 p/th.
